## ArtNet.kt { #artnet-kt }

Art-Net 4 packet encoding and decoding — the wire format only, no sockets.

Art-Net (Artistic Licence, "Art-Net 4 Specification", protocol version 14) carries DMX512 over
UDP port 6454 (`0x1936`). Every packet starts with the 8-byte id `"Art-Net\0"` followed by a
16-bit OpCode sent **low byte first**, as is the `Port` field of an ArtPollReply; the ArtDmx slot
count, and every other multi-byte field here, is sent high byte first. This file implements the
four packets Field uses:

- **ArtDmx** (`0x5000`) — one universe of slot data, 2..512 bytes, even length.
- **ArtSync** (`0x5200`) — "latch the frames you have buffered now", for tear-free multi-universe
  output.
- **ArtPoll** (`0x2000`) / **ArtPollReply** (`0x2100`) — discovery. Field answers ArtPoll as a node
  when it is receiving (see [`DmxInput`](lighting.md#dmxinput-kt-dmxinput)).

Encoders write into a caller-owned `ByteArray` and return the number of bytes written, so a
sender can reuse one buffer per universe for its whole life; nothing on the send path allocates.
Decoders return small immutable values, or `null` for a packet that is not Art-Net or not one of
these OpCodes.

[`PortAddress`](lighting.md#artnet-kt-portaddress) is the 15-bit universe number those packets carry, split Net : SubNet : Universe.
[`DmxOutput`](lighting.md#dmxoutput-kt-dmxoutput) and [`DmxInput`](lighting.md#dmxinput-kt-dmxinput) are built on these codecs; a box reaches them through `artnetOut` and
`artnetIn`. The user-facing page is
[Driving Lights: Art-Net and sACN](../dmx_lighting.md).

## DmxBox.kt { #dmxbox-kt }

Box-scoped ownership of DMX sockets.

Live coding re-runs a box many times and stops it at will; a socket must survive the first and
die with the second. So each `artnetOut` / `sacnOut` / `artnetIn` / `sacnIn` call is keyed by
box and endpoint: a re-run with the same arguments gets the same, still-sending object back (no
rebind, no gap on the wire), different arguments close the old one first, and stopping the box
closes it through `Box.registerStopHook`. Nothing is cached per port for the life of the process,
so a rig stops when the box driving it stops.

Inputs are keyed by protocol and port only, because only one socket can own a UDP port: a second
box asking for the same input shares the first one, and stopping either box closes it (the next
call reopens it).

`artPoll` is the one call here that owns nothing. It sends a single ArtPoll and gathers the
replies for a timeout, which is how to find the nodes on a network before patching to them. The
user-facing page is [Driving Lights: Art-Net and sACN](../dmx_lighting.md).

## DmxInput.kt { #dmxinput-kt }

DMX reception: Field as an Art-Net or sACN node on the network.

[`DmxInput`](lighting.md#dmxinput-kt-dmxinput) binds a UDP port, keeps the most recent frame from every source on every universe, and
merges them on demand. [`MergeMode`](lighting.md#dmxinput-kt-mergemode) chooses highest-takes-precedence or latest-takes-precedence,
under sACN's priority rule, its sequence-number rule ([`SacnSequence`](lighting.md#sacn-kt-sacnsequence)) and both protocols' source
timeouts. `universe(n)` returns the merged 512 slots, `channel(u, c)` a single slot, and
`version(n)` a counter that moves whenever a universe does, which is how a loop or a test waits
for the next frame without sleeping for a guessed interval.

Field also answers the discovery traffic it hears: an ArtPoll gets back an ArtPollReply
describing `ArtNet.NodeInfo`, so consoles and discovery tools list Field alongside real nodes,
and sACN universe-discovery pages from other sources are kept rather than dropped.

What arrived is slots, not colours; [`Fixture`](lighting.md#patch-kt-fixture) `decode` reads a fixture's look back out of them in
its own profile, which is what makes a round trip measurable ([`SceneOnARig`](lighting.md#sceneonarig-kt-sceneonarig)). In a box, use
`artnetIn` or `sacnIn`, which close the socket when the box stops. The user-facing page is
[Driving Lights: Art-Net and sACN](../dmx_lighting.md).

## DmxOutput.kt { #dmxoutput-kt }

DMX transmission: the frame buffers a box writes into, and the thread that puts them on the wire.

[`DmxUniverse`](lighting.md#dmxoutput-kt-dmxuniverse) is one universe of 512 slots, addressed 1-based as consoles and fixture manuals
address them. [`DmxOutput`](lighting.md#dmxoutput-kt-dmxoutput) owns a set of those and a daemon sender thread that ticks at up to
44 Hz, sending a universe whose bytes have changed and re-sending an unchanged one often enough
that no receiver times it out. [`DmxProtocol`](lighting.md#dmxoutput-kt-dmxprotocol) picks the wire format, encoded by [`ArtNet`](lighting.md#artnet-kt-artnet) or
[`Sacn`](lighting.md#sacn-kt-sacn): Art-Net needs a destination host, and sACN goes to each universe's multicast group
unless one is given.

Nothing here waits on Field's frame clock. `beforeTick` runs at the top of each sender tick,
before the universes are snapshotted, which is where [`Patch`](lighting.md#patch-kt-patch) `animate` computes the next look, so
a rig keeps running whether or not a renderer is ticking.

In a box, reach an output through `artnetOut` or `sacnOut` rather than this constructor: those
hand back the same output across re-runs and close it when the box stops. The user-facing page is
[Driving Lights: Art-Net and sACN](../dmx_lighting.md).

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/io/dmx/DmxOutput.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/io/dmx/DmxOutput/)

**Used in:** [A RectSL scene on a light rig](../chain_scene_to_light.md), [Driving Lights: Art-Net and sACN](../dmx_lighting.md)

## DmxVisual.kt { #dmxvisual-kt }

Drawings of a DMX rig and its universes as [`FLine`](graphics.md#fline-kt-fline) geometry, for a box's output or a PNG.

Two views of the same light. [`Patch.toFLines`](lighting.md#dmxvisual-kt--toflines) and [`Box.showPatch`](lighting.md#dmxvisual-kt--showpatch) draw each fixture at its
position in the colour it is set to; [`Patch.receivedToFLines`](lighting.md#dmxvisual-kt--receivedtoflines) and [`Box.showReceived`](lighting.md#dmxvisual-kt--showreceived) draw the
same layout in the colours decoded from what a [`DmxInput`](lighting.md#dmxinput-kt-dmxinput) received, so the sent look and the
arrived one can sit side by side. [`universeToFLines`](lighting.md#dmxvisual-kt--universetoflines) and [`Box.showUniverse`](lighting.md#dmxvisual-kt--showuniverse) show a universe in
wire order instead, as a grid of slots or of fixtures read through a [`FixtureProfile`](lighting.md#patch-kt-fixtureprofile).
[`renderLinesPng`](lighting.md#dmxvisual-kt--renderlinespng) rasterises any of these without a browser.

## Patch.kt { #patch-kt }

A rig as data: what each fixture is, where it sits in DMX space, and where it sits in the room.

A [`Patch`](lighting.md#patch-kt-patch) holds [`Fixture`](lighting.md#patch-kt-fixture)s, each a [`FixtureProfile`](lighting.md#patch-kt-fixtureprofile) (which [`Slot`](lighting.md#patch-kt-slot) sits at every offset from the
start address) at some universe and address, with a position. Addresses are given explicitly or
allocated in runs by `strip`, `stripAlong` and `grid`, which roll over to the next universe
rather than let a fixture straddle slot 512.

Colour goes in through the mappers (`map` from a position and a time, `mapAlong` from distance
along the fixture list, `mapImage` sampled from an [`Img`](imaging.md#imaging-kt-img)) or straight onto a fixture, and goes
out as slot bytes through `render` into a [`DmxOutput`](lighting.md#dmxoutput-kt-dmxoutput). `writeInto` is where a colour becomes
slots: white and amber are taken out of red, green and blue for the profiles that carry them,
gamma is applied, and a 16-bit slot gets its coarse and fine bytes. `decode` inverts that as far
as the slots allow, so a look that came back off the wire can be compared with the one sent.

Positions are the room's, in whatever unit the rig is described in; the mappers and the
`toFLines` drawing work in that unit and nothing here fixes it to metres. `colorTemperature`
turns a black-body temperature into a colour to map onto. The user-facing page is
[Driving Lights: Art-Net and sACN](../dmx_lighting.md).

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/io/dmx/Patch.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/io/dmx/Patch/)

**Used in:** [Driving Lights: Art-Net and sACN](../dmx_lighting.md), [A RectSL scene on a light rig](../chain_scene_to_light.md)

### Slot { #patch-kt-slot }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">enum</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">Slot</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/io/dmx/Patch/#L40)

What one DMX slot of a fixture carries. `_FINE` slots are the low byte of the slot before them.

Constants: `RED`, `GREEN`, `BLUE`, `WHITE`, `AMBER`, `DIMMER`, `RED_FINE`, `GREEN_FINE`, `BLUE_FINE`, `DIMMER_FINE`, `ZERO`, `FULL`.

## Sacn.kt { #sacn-kt }

Streaming ACN (ANSI E1.31-2016, "sACN") packet encoding and decoding — the wire format only.

sACN carries DMX512 universes over UDP port 5568 in three nested ACN PDUs (root layer, framing
layer, DMP layer), each opening with a 16-bit "flags and length" word whose top nibble is `0x7`
and whose low 12 bits count the bytes *from that word to the end of the packet*. All multi-byte
fields are big-endian. This file implements:

- **Data packets** (root vector `0x04`, framing vector `0x02`): 126-byte header plus a START code
  and up to 512 slots — 638 bytes at most.
- **Synchronization packets** (root `0x08`, framing `0x01`, 49 bytes): E1.31 §6.3 universe sync.
  A data packet whose `Synchronization Address` is non-zero is held by receivers until a sync
  packet for that address arrives.
- **Universe discovery packets** (root `0x08`, framing `0x02`, §8): the list of universes a source
  is transmitting, sent every 10 s (`DISCOVERY_INTERVAL_MS`) to universe 64214.

Universes are 1..63999; multicast traffic for universe `u` goes to `239.255.(u >> 8).(u & 0xff)`
(`multicastAddress`). Every source identifies itself by a 16-byte CID (a UUID), which is also how
a receiver tells two sources on the same universe apart for priority and merging.

[`SacnSequence`](lighting.md#sacn-kt-sacnsequence) is the §6.7.2 sequence-number rule a receiver applies per source per universe.
[`DmxOutput`](lighting.md#dmxoutput-kt-dmxoutput) and [`DmxInput`](lighting.md#dmxinput-kt-dmxinput) are built on these codecs; a box reaches them through `sacnOut` and
`sacnIn`. The user-facing page is
[Driving Lights: Art-Net and sACN](../dmx_lighting.md).

## SceneOnARig.kt { #sceneonarig-kt }

A RectSL scene driven onto a light rig over sACN, and measured end to end.

This is the code behind [A RectSL scene on a light rig](../chain_scene_to_light.md): that page,
the demo document and `SceneOnARigTest` all run it rather than describing it, so the rig is
patched one way and measured one way wherever it appears.

The route crosses four parts of Field. A RectSL scene is drawn on the CPU into an [`Img`](imaging.md#imaging-kt-img)
([`RectSLImager`](languages.md#rectslimg-kt-rectslimager)); [`Patch`](lighting.md#patch-kt-patch) `mapImage` colours a 16 × 8 grid of RGB pixels plus four RGBWA washes
from it; a [`DmxOutput`](lighting.md#dmxoutput-kt-dmxoutput) sends those universes as sACN to 127.0.0.1; a [`DmxInput`](lighting.md#dmxinput-kt-dmxinput) receives them,
and [`Fixture`](lighting.md#patch-kt-fixture) `decode` turns what arrived back into colours in the rig's layout, to be compared
with the pixels the rig was given.

Three things are measured, each by a function here: `roundTrip` (what the wire does to each
fixture's colour), `aliasing` (what sampling a 256-pixel frame at 16 points does to a thin moving
line), and `timing` (what a frame costs, and how often the receiver sees one while the scene
animates on the sender's 44 Hz clock).

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/io/dmx/SceneOnARig.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/io/dmx/SceneOnARig/)

The [`LINE`](lighting.md#sceneonarig-kt--sceneonarig--line) scene, drawn in linear light at [`FRAME_W`](lighting.md#sceneonarig-kt--sceneonarig--frame-w) × [`FRAME_H`](lighting.md#sceneonarig-kt--sceneonarig--frame-h), is put on the grid two ways over `frames` frames of the middle 3 seconds (the line wholly on the wall): bilinear point samples of the full frame ([`Patch.mapImage`](lighting.md#patch-kt--patch--mapimage) as it is), and the frame area-averaged to one pixel per fixture first. The line covers a quarter of one column of fixtures, so the light it should put on the rig is `0.25 × ROWS` = 2 fixtures' worth, wherever it is. |
